Skill 1923: imprint circuit design onto wafers: Imprint the electronic circuit design onto the wafers through a process known as photolithography. First, wafers are coated with photosensitive chemicals that harden when exposed to UV light. In sealed dark rooms light is shone through the image of the design through a miniaturising lens and on to the coated wafer. When the chemical is washed off the design remains. The wafers are built up layer by layer, repeating the photo etching process in each new layer. Some layers are cooked, some layers ionised by plasma, and some are baked in metal. Each treatment changes the properties for that layer. Skill: imprint circuit design onto wafers is defined as the process of imprinting the electronic circuit design onto wafers through a method known as photolithography. Imprint circuit design onto wafers involves coating wafers with photosensitive chemicals, exposing them to UV light through a miniaturising lens in sealed dark rooms, and washing away unhardened material so "the design remains." Core components: this includes the sequential "photo etching process" for each layer, with treatments like cooking, ionising by plasma, or baking in metal to change layer properties. Distinctive applications: imprint circuit design onto wafers is applied in semiconductor fabrication to build up wafers "layer by layer" for integrated circuits. Unique value: it enables the precise, multi-layered patterning essential for creating complex microelectronic devices.
